caption:
One blogger logged dictating 182,718 words across 36 apps — and never manually rewrote one of them.

Wispr Flow started as a voice-dictation app, but the part that's making review sites stop and stare is "Command Mode": you highlight text you just said out loud, say something like "make this more concise" or "make this sound more formal," and it rewrites itself. No keyboard. No highlighting-and-retyping. Just talking to your draft like it's a person who takes notes.

Underneath that is AI Auto-Edits, quietly stripping filler words, fixing punctuation, and formatting lists as you speak — in Slack, email, ChatGPT, Claude, docs, basically anywhere you'd normally type. And it's grown past dictation entirely: there's now a Notetaker product on Mac that turns your meetings into notes without you lifting a finger.

It's not flawless everywhere — Windows users have reported some rough edges (occasional freezing in apps like VS Code, and Flow re-adding itself to startup after being disabled), so Mac is currently the smoother ride. But the sheer amount of independent, hands-on coverage this thing has racked up in the last couple months says it's doing something real, not just marketing itself well.

If you've ever wished you could just say the edit instead of making it — this is worth five minutes of your curiosity.

slides.heading: Say It. Watch It Rewrite Itself.
slides.body: No keyboard, no click — just talk, and the text changes in front of you.

slides.heading: The Type-Then-Edit Loop
slides.body: Draft it, then go back and fix run-ons, delete every "um," clean up punctuation, reformat the list. Everyone does this loop for emails, Slack, and docs — every single time.

slides.heading: Command Mode: Voice-Edited Text
slides.body: Highlight what you just dictated, say "make this more concise" or "make this sound more formal," and it rewrites in place — no typing, no undo-redo dance.

slides.heading: It Cleans Up As You Talk
slides.body: AI Auto-Edits strip filler words, fix punctuation, and format lists in real time — in Slack, email, ChatGPT, Claude, docs, anywhere there's a text field.

slides.heading: Meeting Notes You Never Typed
slides.body: Notetaker sits alongside Flow on Mac, turning conversations into notes without you lifting a finger — dictation grown into something bigger.

slides.heading: The Honest Catch
slides.body: Windows users report rough edges — occasional freezing in apps like VS Code, and Flow re-adding itself to startup even after being disabled. Mac is the more polished experience right now.
